title: RunState
description:
Durable state of an AgentRun workflow (RUN-001/RUN-004). This is the shape checkpointed by Temporal at each superstep; it must remain serializable and must never contain a chain-of-thought field.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY IMPLEMENTED, stated because this document described a shape nothing emitted and three code comments cited it as the contract for GET /runs/{run_id}. Measured 2026-10-08: `graph_cursor` and `no_progress_counter` appear NOWHERE in the repository outside this file, and the status endpoint returns `workflow_id`/`status`/`paused`/`pending_approval`/`budgets_consumed`/`failure` — not this document. `status`, `pending_approval`, `budgets_consumed` and `failure` are real and shared with that endpoint; the rest is design that has no producer yet. A schema nobody implements is not a contract, and pretending otherwise is how a consumer builds against a field that will never arrive.

agent_manifest_ref.description: name@version of the AgentManifest driving this run.

status.description: PAUSED is an operator-initiated pause (RUN-001, Run Controller); PAUSED_FOR_APPROVAL is a run blocked on a specific approval decision (RUN-005) — distinct because only the latter carries pending_approval.

graph_cursor.description: Position in the graph runtime (RUN-002): which node(s) are active/pending per branch.

activity_calls.description: VRT-AEON-001: kind=activity nodes that actually ran. Counted after policy and approval, so a node refused by either is never counted as if it had run.

tool_call_hash.description: Hash of bound parameters; an approval only applies if this matches at execution time.

no_progress_counter.description: Consecutive supersteps without new evidence/state change; hard-stops runaway loops.

failure.description: Why the run ended badly (OBS-011). ABSENT unless something went wrong in a way `status` cannot express, and absent for CANCELLED — a Temporal cancellation carries no reason, so a failure object there would exist to say nothing. Asked for by Veritium as a second-consumer note: a reconciliator could see THAT a run failed and not WHY.

kind.description: The distinction `status` loses: it maps Temporal's FAILED, TIMED_OUT and TERMINATED onto one FAILED, because this schema's status enum has one value for all three and widening it would break every consumer that switches on it. A workflow that raised an error, one that ran out of time and one an operator killed are three incidents with three next actions.

message.description: The ROOT CAUSE's message, not the outermost one — measured: an activity failure's outer message is the literal string 'activity error' and the useful text is one level down. For a termination it is the operator's reason. Passed through from the workflow unchanged, so whoever writes an activity owns what lands here: a failure message is the obvious back door for the chain-of-thought this document forbids.

type.description: The application error type when the failure carries one (BudgetExceeded, PolicyDenied). The workflow's own vocabulary, so a consumer can branch without parsing a message.

activity.description: Which activity failed, when the failure came from one. It sits at the OUTER level of the cause chain while the message sits at the inner.

retryable.description: Three states and not two: present and false (Temporal said non-retryable), present and true, or ABSENT because the failure carried no application info to say either. An absent value is not a false one.

terminated_by.description: Temporal's `identity` on a termination: a worker or CLI identity string, NOT an authenticated Aeon caller. Named for what it is, because nothing here proves who the person was.
